content.text: The atlas tools were denied, so I'll search the code directly.

Changing `TelegramLinkWidget`'s props affects two pages. The widget lives at `app/portal/components/TelegramLinkWidget.tsx`. I used a text search because the atlas tools were denied, so a dynamic import or re-export under another name would not have shown up.

**Pages**
- `/portal/supplier` (`app/portal/supplier/page.tsx:715`) renders `<TelegramLinkWidget role="supplier" />`.
- `/portal/reseller` (`app/portal/reseller/page.tsx:741`) renders `<TelegramLinkWidget role="reseller" />`.

Both pass only a `role` prop today. If you add a required prop, both call sites need updating. Renaming or removing `role`, or changing its allowed values, breaks both.

**Tests**
- `test/portal-telegram-widget.test.ts` builds the widget with `{ role: "reseller" }` and `{ role: "supplier" }`. It also checks that both pages embed the widget, so prop changes could break it.

The widget also calls `/api/v2/auth/telegram/status`, `/link-token` and `/unlink`. Changing its props doesn't change those routes. It would only matter if the new props change the request payloads.
